A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OST/Orlicz-EPT research despite the changed title and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime comparisons and SVM classification experiments on four document datasets, Orbit and MPEG7, including appendix results for GLog.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds parameter-sensitivity results on TWITTER and MPEG7 in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The balanced-measure construction, calibrated cost, OST objective, univariate computation and Orlicz-EPT binary-search procedure are retained. Added proofs and graph-handling explanations do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TWITTER, RECIPE, CLASSIC, AMAZON, Orbit and MPEG7 using GLog and GSqrt. The added parameter sweeps retain these data and task requirements; no new dataset, domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain UOT, d0-Tree and regEPT-Tree for classification, and Orlicz-EPT for timing. v2 discusses debiased UOT using results explicitly attributed to earlier work, without adding it to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds experiments with b equal to 0.5 or 2 and alpha equal to 0.1 or 0.2, supplementing the original b=1 and alpha=0 setting. The original evaluation settings remain unchanged; the newly described inner validation split is additional documentation, not evidence of a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds targeted sensitivity checks for b and alpha across three Phi choices on TWITTER and MPEG7 with both graph types, reported in Tables 2-9. These examine parameter dependence within existing experiments rather than introducing a broad robustness or failure-analysis program.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten outer train/test repeats and display error bars. v2 additionally discloses ten repeats for inner validation and explicitly identifies standard deviations in the sensitivity tables. There is no stated increase in outer repetitions or addition of significance tests.

E6.justification: The six original result plots are retained, including the reported timing advantages of at least 250x, 13800x and 11200x. Tables 2-9 add parameter-specific accuracies, such as 72.64 ± 0.50 for TWITTER/GSqrt with Phi2 and alpha=0.1. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 3.1 and its proof of the previously asserted EPT/OT equivalence, explicitly restricts lambda to be nonnegative, and supplies a graph-wide Hölder bound. Most other propositions are retained or relocated. B.2 also adds an overbroad OW-reduction assertion: for identical unit point masses with Phi(t)=t² and b=lambda=w1=w2=1, Equation (8) gives sqrt(2)-2, whereas OW is zero.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list now explicitly include theoretical foundations enabling binary-search computation of Orlicz-EPT. This modestly expands the stated contributions; the central claims about efficient OST, transport connections, orders-of-magnitude speedups and preliminary application benefits remain.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 substantially expands applicability and limitations: fixed versus learned graph metrics, shortest-path uniqueness, supports on edges, selection of Phi, and properties potentially lost when replacing OW with OST. v2 also interprets parameter tuning and softens the TDA conclusion from asserting helpfulness to suggesting possible benefit.

D1.justification: v2 reports a code release and repository address, supplies dataset-access instructions, and documents graph clustering, edge sampling, connectivity construction and inner validation. These materially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit word2vec/Google News specification, and its hardware disclosure remains only 'commodity hardware'.

R1.justification: Sections 6 and B.2 substantially broaden positioning beyond the earlier GST/EPT discussion to graph comparison, graph kernels, variational Sobolev IPMs, sliced/tree-sliced transport and debiased UOT. Numerous corresponding works are newly cited; these are substantive additions rather than bibliography-format changes.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and explanatory narrative are extensively rewritten. Orlicz-EPT and OST receive separate sections, theoretical material is redistributed between the main text and appendix, and the appendices are reorganized into reviews, discussions and experiments. Acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added.

P2.justification: The paper adopts a substantially different NeurIPS layout, including a redesigned title block and resized, repositioned displays. Existing classification plots move alongside their experimental sections, Table 1 moves to the appendix, and v2 adds a graph illustration and eight sensitivity tables. The original six plots themselves are reused.

improvement.justification: The added EPT/OT proof, graph and validation details, code pointer and parameter studies make the existing contribution easier to assess and reproduce. The gain is limited because the method and original benchmark evidence remain unchanged. Benefits are partly offset by lost embedding specificity and the new, overbroad equal-mass Orlicz-EPT/OW equivalence assertion in Appendix B.2.
